---

A genome-overview circle places each chromosome as a sector and stacks one **ring per track**: GC content, repeat/gene density, per-sample expression, SNPs — any per-window genomic signal \[1\]. The reference builds this in Perl Circos with a karyotype file plus a config per ring; this tutorial reproduces the composite self-contained in R with **circlize** on simulated chromosomes:

## Example

![](../images/CircosPlot_demo.png){fig-alt="Genome Overview Circle DEMO" fig-align="center" width="60%"}

## Setup

-   System Requirements: Cross-platform (Linux/MacOS/Windows)

-   Programming language: R

-   Dependent packages: `circlize`

```{r packages setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, output=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(circlize))
```

```{r}
sessioninfo::session_info("attached")
```

## Data Preparation

9 simulated chromosomes (29-207 Mb) cut into 2-Mb windows; per-window GC content, transposable-element density, gene number/density, RPKM for two samples (sample 2 carries planted arm-level gains on Chr3/Chr8) and heterozygous/homozygous SNP calls. Real data follow the same `chr, start, end, value` format the source document feeds to Circos:

```{r load data}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(circlize))
set.seed(1401)
## 9 simulated chromosomes
chr_len <- c(118, 98, 207, 50, 45, 36, 29, 196, 56) * 1e6
chrs <- paste0("Chr", 1:9)
binsize <- 2e6
tracks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(chrs), function(i) {
  nb <- chr_len[i] %/% binsize
  data.frame(chr = chrs[i], start = (0:(nb - 1)) * binsize, end = (1:nb) * binsize)
}))
nb <- nrow(tracks)
tracks$GC <- pmin(0.5, pmax(0.25, 0.37 + 0.05 * sin(seq(0, 40, length.out = nb)) + rnorm(nb, 0, 0.025)))
tracks$TE  <- pmin(0.9, pmax(0.05, 0.45 + 0.18 * sin(seq(0, 25, length.out = nb) + 2) + rnorm(nb, 0, 0.07)))
tracks$gene_num <- pmax(0, rpois(nb, 12 + 10 * sin(seq(0, 30, length.out = nb))))
tracks$gene_pct <- pmin(0.55, tracks$gene_num / 60)
tracks$RPKM1 <- exp(rnorm(nb, log(3), 1.1))                # sample 1
tracks$RPKM2 <- exp(rnorm(nb, log(3), 1.1))                # sample 2
tracks$RPKM2 <- tracks$RPKM2 * ifelse(tracks$chr %in% c("Chr3", "Chr8"), 2.4, 1)  # arm-level gain
snp <- tracks[sample(nb, 360), ]
snp$type <- factor(sample(c("het", "hom"), 360, TRUE, prob = c(0.7, 0.3)))
snp$v <- ifelse(snp$type == "het", 0.35, 0.75) + runif(360, -0.08, 0.08)
```

## Visualization

### 1. The Genome Circle

Eight rings over the nine chromosomes: ideograms with names, GC content line (pink), TE density heatmap (magma), gene density heatmap (blue-red), gene number line (green), two per-sample RPKM tracks (orange/purple — the Chr3/Chr8 elevation is the planted gain) and SNP points (black het, red hom):

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.1GenomeCircos
#| fig-cap: "Genome-overview circos of 9 simulated chromosomes with 8 stacked rings: chromosome ideograms, GC content line, TE density heatmap, gene density heatmap, gene number line, per-sample RPKM tracks (sample 2 shows planted Chr3/Chr8 gains) and het/hom SNP points."
#| out.width: "90%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 9.5
#| fig-height: 9.5

circos.par(start.degree = 90, gap.degree = 1.5, track.margin = c(0.004, 0.004),
           cell.padding = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
circos.initialize(factors = factor(tracks$chr, levels = chrs),
                  xlim = cbind(rep(0, 9), chr_len))
## track 1: chromosome ideograms + names
circos.track(ylim = c(0, 1), track.height = 0.06, bg.col = "grey90", bg.border = "grey40",
             panel.fun = function(x, y) {
               sn <- get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
               circos.text(get.cell.meta.data("xlim")[1] + 3e6, 0.5, sn,
                           facing = "bending.inside", niceFacing = TRUE, cex = 0.55, adj = c(0, 0.5))
             })
## track 2: GC content line
circos.track(ylim = c(0.2, 0.55), track.height = 0.09, bg.border = "grey70",
             panel.fun = function(x, y) {
               sn <- get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
               d <- tracks[tracks$chr == sn, ]
               circos.lines((d$start + d$end) / 2, d$GC, col = "#F781BF", lwd = 1.1)
             })
## track 3: TE density heatmap
circos.track(ylim = c(0, 1), track.height = 0.09, bg.border = NA,
             panel.fun = function(x, y) {
               sn <- get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
               d <- tracks[tracks$chr == sn, ]
               col_te <- colorRamp2(c(0.05, 0.5, 0.9), c("#440154", "#FCA50A", "#FDE725"))
               circos.rect(d$start, 0, d$end, 1, col = col_te(d$TE), border = NA)
             })
## track 4: gene density heatmap
circos.track(ylim = c(0, 1), track.height = 0.09, bg.border = NA,
             panel.fun = function(x, y) {
               sn <- get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
               d <- tracks[tracks$chr == sn, ]
               col_g <- colorRamp2(c(0, 0.27, 0.55), c("#2166AC", "#F7F7F7", "#B2182B"))
               circos.rect(d$start, 0, d$end, 1, col = col_g(d$gene_pct), border = NA)
             })
## track 5: gene number line
circos.track(ylim = c(0, max(tracks$gene_num)), track.height = 0.08, bg.border = "grey70",
             panel.fun = function(x, y) {
               sn <- get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
               d <- tracks[tracks$chr == sn, ]
               circos.lines((d$start + d$end) / 2, d$gene_num, col = "#1B7837", lwd = 1.1)
             })
## tracks 6-7: RPKM per sample
col_rp <- c("#E08214", "#8073AC")
for (s in 1:2) {
  v <- if (s == 1) tracks$RPKM1 else tracks$RPKM2
  circos.track(ylim = c(0, max(c(tracks$RPKM1, tracks$RPKM2))), track.height = 0.08,
               bg.border = "grey70",
               panel.fun = function(x, y) {
                 sn <- get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
                 d <- tracks[tracks$chr == sn, ]
                 circos.lines((d$start + d$end) / 2, v[tracks$chr == sn], col = col_rp[s], lwd = 1.1)
               })
}
## track 8: SNP points
circos.track(ylim = c(0, 1), track.height = 0.08, bg.border = "grey70",
             panel.fun = function(x, y) {
               sn <- get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
               d <- snp[snp$chr == sn, ]
               circos.points((d$start + d$end) / 2, d$v, pch = 16, cex = 0.35,
                             col = ifelse(d$type == "het", "black", "#D7301F"))
             })
circos.clear()
par(xpd = NA)
legend("center", legend = c("GC content", "TE density", "Gene density", "Gene number",
                            "RPKM sample 1", "RPKM sample 2", "SNP het", "SNP hom"),
       col = c("#F781BF", "#FCA50A", "#B2182B", "#1B7837", col_rp, "black", "#D7301F"),
       pch = c(NA, 15, 15, NA, NA, NA, 16, 16), lwd = c(1.5, NA, NA, 1.5, 1.5, 1.5, NA, NA),
       bty = "n", cex = 0.62, ncol = 2, x.intersp = 1.2)
```

::: callout-tip
**Practice tips**

-   Keep **one binned `tracks` data frame** and subset it per ring inside `panel.fun` — per-ring data frames with different row orders desynchronize positions across rings.
-   Ring order is outside-in by construction; put the identity tracks (ideogram, GC) outside and the sample tracks inside, then call `circos.clear()` **before** the legend or base graphics are captured inside the last ring.
-   For a real karyotype, read cytoband widths from an Ensembl/UCSC table instead of faking chromosome lengths; the rest of the code is unchanged.
:::

## Applications

::: {#fig-CircosPlotApplications1}
![](../images/CircosPlot_demo.png){fig-alt="Genome overview circle" fig-align="center" width="60%"}

Genome overview circle
:::

The same ring stack serves any per-window genome tracks: methylation, chromatin accessibility, conservation, or CNV log-ratio across a pangenome or a single chromosome of interest.

\[2\] Krzywinski M, Schein J, Birol I, et al. Circos: an information aesthetic for comparative genomics. Genome Res. 2009;19(9):1639-1645. doi:10.1101/gr.092759.109
